## Spec rules confirmed live

- 37 accepts then 429 with `retry_after_ms: 41`; gold: 74 accepts then 429 with `retry_after_ms: 21` (refill window stays 1500 ms, so rate scales with burst).
- One exact `1500/37 ms` step turns a rejection into an accept — the tolerance in `TOKEN_EPSILON` keeps float clock arithmetic from stealing a token.
- `vendor/` and `limiter/__init__.py` byte-identical to HEAD; no commit made (not requested).

## One judgement call to flag

The spec doesn't state the type of `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, so I return an **int** (the natural Python form of "tokens left after this request"). If the gateway layer needs string headers, it's a one-line change in `middleware.check_request`.

Also note `check_request` keeps buckets in process memory (the signature has no state parameter), and `limiter.middleware.reset_buckets()` drops them — used by the test fixture.
